articles.title: Where there's a will, there's an Agra Expressway: How Akhilesh will fund SP poll promises
articles.summary: Lucknow: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday said his party had worked out a financial roadmap for implementing its promises in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, asserting that the availability of funds would not be an obstacle if there was political will. Asked how the party proposed to finance its poll promises and where the revenue would come from, Yadav said he had prepared a separate document detailing how funds would be arranged for the schemes planned over five years, within the state's annual budget of around Rs 1 lakh crore. He said senior officials with experience in financial and administrative matters had been involved in the exercise to assess the feasibility of major decisions and schemes. Citing the Agra-Lucknow Expressway as an example, Yadav said his government had initially considered building the 302-km project under the public-private partnership (PPP) model, but banks were not extending the required support, delaying its progress. "After discussions with officials, we decided that if the expressway had to be built, its model would have to be changed," he said, adding that it was subsequently constructed through the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) model using the government's own budget. The project cost around Rs 15,000 crore, he said. Yadav also cited the distribution of laptops and the development of metro networks in Lucknow, Agra, Kanpur and the Noida-Greater Noida region as examples of projects delivered by his government. Taking a swipe at the BJP government, he questioned its infrastructure spending and alleged irregularities in the tendering process for projects, including the Gorakhpur Link Expressway. Referring to alleged allocation of tenders worth more than Rs 16,000 crore, he asked, "Where is the shortage of money?" "When there is a will, there is a way," he said. On the proposed restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) for government employees, Yadav acknowledged the technical complications involving funds deposited under the National Pension System (NPS). He said the party would constitute a committee involving experienced finance officials to work out the modalities. "We had given this assurance in 2022 as well, and we reiterate it: the Old Pension Scheme will be implemented for government employees," he said. Asked what would guarantee jobs for young people if the INDIA bloc came to power in Uttar Pradesh, Yadav cited the establishment of the SCL institution as an example of how investment could create local employment. 'Modi forced into silence after UP stopped his chariot’: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge He said families had welcomed the institution because their children would no longer have to move elsewhere for jobs, and alleged that the BJP government had not acknowledged the project as one initiated by the SP government. On attracting further investments such as Samsung's manufacturing facility in Noida, Yadav said his government had engaged with the company's officials and incorporated the facilities and incentives they sought, despite competition from other states. He also listed power projects established or taken forward during the SP government's tenure, including those at Etah, Harduaganj, Panki and Lalitpur, and said his government had framed a solar energy policy. He alleged that the BJP government had not set up a power plant in its 10 years in office. Speaking about support for traditional weavers, Yadav said the proposed government would provide skill development, market access and dedicated budgetary assistance. He also promised financial support for modernisation and said clusters could be developed to strengthen the sector. He said the party would revive the initiative started by his father and SP founder Mulayam Singh Yadav to provide electricity to weavers at fixed rates.

articles.title: Fake job offers, seized passports: Inside Delhi's international human trafficking, cyber fraud racket
articles.summary: New Delhi: Lured to India with promises of lucrative jobs, 164 foreign nationals from Indonesia and Malaysia allegedly found themselves trapped in a network of human trafficking and cybercrooks, with their passports seized upon arrival, movement restricted and lives reduced to making fraudulent calls to people back home, Delhi Police said on Thursday. Kept in paying guest (PG) accommodations, allegedly served substandard food and subjected to physical assault if they refused to work, the foreign nationals were forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in their own countries through fraudulent investment platforms, police said. In a major crackdown in Noida's Sector 136, on an alleged international human trafficking and cyber fraud network, the Crime Branch of Delhi Police has rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from premises allegedly being used to operate the racket. A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, has been arrested in connection with the case. According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India, promising attractive salaries and better career prospects. However, their ordeal allegedly began soon after they landed in the country. Their passports were taken away upon arrival, leaving them without control over their identity documents and restricting their ability to leave, police said. They were subsequently shifted to PG accommodations and allegedly forced to work to cheat others. Those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities were allegedly thrashed by members of the network to ensure compliance, a senior police officer said, adding that so far they got to know that around two people were thrashed. Supreme Court orders 'victim protection plan' implementation to combat human trafficking, survivor rehabilitation The living conditions at the accommodations were also allegedly poor, with the foreign nationals being provided substandard food. Despite a fleet of around 40 cabs being used to ferry them between the PG accommodations and the cyber fraud call centre, they were not allowed to venture out independently or move around as they wished, the officer said. "The cabs were allegedly deployed to transport them to the call centre and bring them back to their accommodations, ensuring that their movement remained under the control of the handlers," the officer said. The foreign nationals were not merely made to operate computers and mobile phones but were allegedly trained to execute a specific pattern of cyber fraud. They were provided written scripts containing conversations thatthey had to follow while approaching prospective victims. The targets were primarily people in Malaysia and Indonesia. The operators allegedly created fictitious female identities and social media profiles to establish contact with unsuspecting individuals. "Using these profiles, the foreign nationals were instructed to initiate conversations, develop online relationships and gradually gain the confidence of their targets. Once trust was established, the victims were persuaded to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms," the officer added. The syndicate allegedly used websites and APK-based applications to lure people with promises of high returns. The victims were made to believe that they were investing in legitimate financial opportunities, while the money was allegedly siphoned off through the fraudulent network. "We got to know about the fraud after the crime branch received an email alert about the alleged racket around a week ago, following which its officers began developing intelligence about the network," the officer said. Special Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) HGS Dhaliwal said, "As soon as we received information about the cyber racket, I personally constituted a specialised team and directed the officers to take immediate action." Initial information suggested that around 60 to 70 foreign nationals were being held and forced to work in the cyber fraud operation. However, when the police team conducted the operation at the suspected premises, the actual number turned out to be significantly higher. The operation led to the rescue of 164 foreign nationals, exposing the scale of the alleged racket. The police are now investigating how the foreign nationals were recruited, who facilitated their travel to India, and how their passports were taken away. "During the entire investigation, two names -- Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati -- cropped up. Bhati used to arrange the PG accommodations and transportation facilities. Both are absconding, both will be arrested soon," the officer said. Certain bank accounts allegedly maintained by Kumar and Bhati have been identified as being used to meet rental and other operational expenses of the network. The financial trail is being examined to establish the flow of money, identify the beneficiaries and trace the proceeds generated through the alleged cyber fraud. The arrested Malaysian national, Tan Guan Wei, a resident of Negeri Sembilan, is being questioned about his alleged role in the network, his association with other members and the extent of his involvement in operating the fraudulent platforms. The police have seized a substantial digital infrastructure allegedly used to run the operation. The recoveries include 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports. Of the 355 mobile phones, 335 were old or used handsets and 20 were new phones in sealed packaging. The 53 SIM cards include 31 international and 22 Indian connections. The recovered passports comprise 95 Indonesian and 79 Malaysian documents. Servers and other electronic material have also been seized. Investigators are examining the devices to identify the victims, establish the communication channels used by the syndicate and trace financial transactions linked to the fraudulent platforms. Special CP Dhaliwal further said the conditions in which the foreign nationals were being held were deplorable. Praising the team for its work, Dhaliwal added, "Our team has done a commendable job in this case. We will extend all possible assistance to the rescued foreigners and ensure that they can return to their respective countries safely." A case has been registered at the Crime Branch police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway to identify other members of the international network and establish the extent of the alleged human trafficking and cyber fraud operation. The officer further said that over 10 teams have been formed to nab those who are absconding. "Teams are conducting search in many states, including Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Punjab, Rajasthan and many other area. Important leads were also received about the whereabouts of Bhati and Kumar. They will be nabbed soon," the officer added.
